name: Belize
prevalence_note: In October 2026 the Central Bank of Belize warned that callers posing as its staff, some inviting people into Google Meet sessions, were asking for passwords, PINs and card details; the same month it named an unlicensed lending service in a separate warning notice.
cross_border_note: Belize numbers have seven digits after +501; impostors often move the victim from a voice call into a video-meeting link or a messaging app, so the visible number says little about where the caller is.

scams.name: Fake Central Bank of Belize caller
scams.name_en: Caller claiming to represent the Central Bank of Belize asks for banking credentials, sometimes over Google Meet
scams.signals_en: Unsolicited call or meeting invite from someone saying they work for the Central Bank of Belize, asking for passwords, PINs, card numbers or other banking details.
scams.legit_en: The Central Bank of Belize states it does not make unsolicited calls asking the public for banking credentials, passwords, PINs or card information.
bait_tactics: My bank told me to deal with these matters only at the branch counter, so I'll go there tomorrow.
I don't join meetings from numbers I don't know; send me the official letter by post.

scams.name: Unlicensed quick-loan offer
scams.name_en: Easy-loan service operating without a Central Bank licence
scams.signals_en: A lender advertising fast, easy loans that does not appear among institutions licensed under Belize's Moneylenders Act; the Central Bank issued a warning notice naming one such service.
scams.legit_en: Licensed lenders in Belize are supervised by the Central Bank and can be checked on its lists of regulated institutions before any money changes hands.
bait_tactics: Give me your licence number and I'll look it up on the Central Bank's site first.
I only borrow from my credit union.
